runs.title: Depardieu drops his appeal: what he said and the sentence
runs.prompt: The French actor Gérard Depardieu was convicted of sexual assault; on 16 November 2026 it was reported that he has dropped his appeal against the conviction. Find out from news coverage: (1) what sentence he was originally given and which court convicted him, (2) what Depardieu said in his statement about dropping the appeal (including any apology), and (3) whether he now accepts the guilt. Use only public, non-paywalled pages. Start at the BBC article on the story and try other outlets if needed.
runs.answer: Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 by a Paris court (the Paris criminal court) of sexually assaulting a 55-year-old set dresser and a 35-year-old assistant director on the set of Les Volets Verts in September 2021, and was given an 18-month suspended prison sentence, with his name to go on France's sex-offender register and €1,000 compensation paid to each woman for the way his defence treated them; the suspended sentence now stands with his appeal withdrawn. In his written statement he said: "I was found guilty. I hear it and I accept this conviction," and, apologising to the victims for the first time, "I address my deep and sincere apologies to those who suffered." He added that on film sets he had "hidden behind provocation and ribald humour," that he had "come to understand that intention changes nothing about the harm caused," and that he belonged "to a world that no longer exists." So yes — he now publicly accepts the guilty verdict and apologises, dropping his long-standing denial (though the wording accepts the conviction rather than describing the acts in detail).

runs.prompt: Irish boxer Lee Reeves has died at the age of 31, with tributes being paid. runs.answer: Limerick boxer Lee "El Champo" Reeves, 31, of Roxboro, Limerick, died on Monday 16 November 2026 at University Hospital Limerick, surrounded by his family, three and a half months after being knocked out by Gary Cully in a pro fight at Dublin's 3Arena on 1 August 2026. He was stretchered from the ring with a catastrophic brain injury, had major brain surgery and was placed in an induced coma at Beaumont Hospital (later reported as moving to the Mater before transfer to UHL to be near his family), and is understood to have contracted an infection while recovering. Tributes are public and non-paywalled: his friend and former coach Jonathan O'Brien — who ran the GoFundMe and posted regular updates — wrote on Facebook "Goodbye son, sleep tight, you fought so hard til the end"; his sister Jessie wrote on social media "I'll see you on the other side my brother… I love you endlessly El Champo"; Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention, of which he was an ambassador, posted a tribute on Facebook; and Limerick Fianna Fáil councillor Catherine Slattery (who gave him a civic reception) paid tribute in the Limerick Post and Irish Examiner. runs.title: Richard Tice lobbied the Bank of England on crypto: the claim
runs.prompt: Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice is reported to have lobbied the Bank of England on cryptocurrency after a £9m donation. Find out from public UK news pages: (1) what exactly Tice is claimed to have done and when, (2) the size and source of the donation involved, and (3) whether Tice or Reform have responded. Use non-paywalled sources where possible; note if a source is paywalled.
runs.answer: Per The i Paper (13 Nov 2026, free to read), Richard Tice wrote to Sam Woods, chief executive of the Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority, on 27 November 2025 asking for "light touch" regulation of stablecoins/crypto, warning Britain was losing business to the US (citing the GENIUS Act and over $250bn of dollar-backed stablecoin issuance); he wrote again on 17 December 2025 to Woods and deputy governor Sarah Breeden saying a "light touch regulatory framework" was essential to keep the UK a leader, and he and Farage had met Governor Andrew Bailey in September 2025 to discuss crypto. The £9m came from cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne (reported 12% stake in Tether, issuer of USDT) and was received four months before the November 2025 letter — at the time the largest single donation to a UK party by a living donor (Harborne and Ben Delo later gave £36m each in September 2026, and Farage earlier took a £5m personal gift from Harborne). Tice responded that his intervention was consistent with his longstanding support for financial deregulation, saying he had been "shouting from the rooftops" to deregulate the financial sector; the Bank said it supported stablecoi
